title: Engineer, Staff_Customer Engineering_Power&Thermal
description:
**Company:**
------------

Qualcomm India Private Limited
**Job Area:**
-------------

Engineering Group, Engineering Group \> Software Applications Engineering
**General Summary:**

**JOB OVERVIEW**

This position is part of the Qualcomm Customer Engineering Group, which collaborates closely with partners and customers — from concept through commercialization — across Qualcomm's broad Snapdragon platform portfolio. The team supports all aspects of embedded software including hardware and software architecture, feature prototyping, feature integration, software customization, performance and power optimization, system validation, and complex debugging efforts critical to product launch.


This is a Staff\-level Customer Engineering position focused on Power and Thermal software, system power management, and low\-power architecture across a wide range of Qualcomm Snapdragon platforms and operating environments — including Android, Linux (LV/Yocto), QNX, and multi\-OS virtualized stacks (e.g., HGY, HQX, and other product families).


The role provides technical leadership in troubleshooting complex customer issues, defining application\-level power and thermal solutions, developing design recommendations, and driving resolution across HLOS, non\-HLOS, hypervisor, chipset, and customer engineering teams. Key technical focus areas include Suspend to RAM (S2R), Dynamic Sleep, PCM, thermal management, subsystem power states, and system suspend/resume flows.  



**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

 **Power \& Thermal Technical Leadership**

* Lead troubleshooting of complex Power and Thermal software issues across multiple Snapdragon platforms and OS environments (Android, Linux, QNX, and others).
* Provide technical leadership for customer issues involving:
* Power management features – S2R, Dynamic Sleep / DSQB, PCM, and other low\-power modes
* Thermal management and TDP workload characterization across product families
* Device and subsystem power states (AOP, RPMh, LPASS/ADSP, DSPs, NSP)
* Virtual\-machine and hypervisor power interactions in multi\-OS automotive and compute platforms
* Analyse system\-wide power management flows across HLOS and non\-HLOS components, including Linux, Android, QNX, TrustZone, AOP, DSPs, hypervisor, and platform hardware.
* Apply strong knowledge of Linux and Android Power Management frameworks to influence customer application design and investigate power management issues.

Understand and debug the role of hypervisors in automotive and compute power management, including host/guest interactions, VM lifecycle management, resource ownership, and inter\-VM power coordination.  

* 

**️ Architecture \& Customer Engagement**

* Provide power and thermal design recommendations for customer applications, workloads, and system architectures across Snapdragon platform families.
* Participate in technical discussions with customers, chipset power teams, thermal systems teams, architecture teams, product managers, and regional CE organizations.
* Translate customer requirements into clear internal software, system, and architecture requirements.
* Lead root\-cause analysis, issue reproduction, log analysis, system characterization, and corrective action planning.
* Provide customer\-specific software recommendations, patches, workarounds, and implementation guidance.

Represent Qualcomm in technical discussions with customers and Tier\-1/Tier\-2 partners from initial requirements through feature implementation and product launch.  

* 

 **Characterization \& Measurement**

* Perform power and thermal characterization for platform\-specific workloads including AI, multimedia, connectivity, and automotive TDP use cases.
* Analyse performance\-versus\-power behaviour for customer\-specific AI networks and platform workloads, including NSP/DSP and HLOS processing pipelines.
* Support the development and validation of workload and loading tools, tuning monitoring tools to represent realistic product use cases.
* Provide accurate power measurement data and technical analysis to chipset power, PPAT, and thermal systems teams.

Leverage hardware\-level data and SoC registers for power characterization, debug, and APDP generation across target platforms.  

* 

 **Knowledge Sharing \& Mentorship**

* Conduct technical training and workshops for customers, partners, CE teams, and internal engineering organizations.
* Develop debug guides, architecture documentation, training materials, and reusable technical content on power and thermal topics across OS and platform families.
* Mentor and guide junior and early\-career engineers on Power and Thermal software, system debugging, customer engagement, and technical analysis.
* Influence architecture and feature improvements by providing feedback based on hands\-on customer and platform experience.

Scale technical knowledge through creation of reusable diagnostics, debug methodologies, and issue\-tracking artifacts applicable across platforms.  

* 

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

**Education \& Experience**

* B.E./B.Tech in Engineering, Computer Science, Electronics, or related field with 8\+ years of Software Applications Engineering, Embedded Systems, or related experience.
* OR M.Tech/M.S. in relevant field with 6\+ years of experience.

OR Ph.D. in relevant field with 4\+ years of experience.  

* 

**Required Skills**

* 3\+ years of experience in a customer\-facing technical role.
* 3\+ years of experience with C, C\+\+, Python, or similar programming languages.
* 3\+ years of experience with embedded software debugging and system\-level issue resolution.
* Strong understanding of Linux or Android Power Management fundamentals.
* Hands\-on experience troubleshooting embedded software across HLOS and non\-HLOS components.
* Experience with at least one embedded/real\-time OS: Linux, Android, QNX, or another RTOS.
* Experience with system suspend, resume, shutdown, wakeup, or low\-power features.
* Experience working with multitasking operating systems and embedded system architecture.
* Experience analysing logs, traces, performance data, and power or thermal measurement results.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Demonstrated ability to work effectively with customers and cross\-functional engineering teams.

Demonstrated technical leadership, mentoring, and problem\-solving skills.  

* 

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Staff\-level experience leading complex customer issues across multiple engineering organizations.
* Deep understanding of Linux kernel power management frameworks and system suspend/resume flows.
* Experience with Qualcomm Snapdragon Power and Thermal software across one or more OS environments: Android, Linux (LV/Yocto), QNX.
* Experience with low\-power features: S2R, DSQB/Dynamic Sleep, PCM, runtime power management, and power\-domain control.
* Experience with non\-HLOS power management components: TrustZone, AOP, RPMh, power management firmware, and related system services.
* Experience with hypervisors and virtualization in automotive or compute embedded systems (e.g., QNX\-based MGVM/Flex configurations, Android GVM, multi\-OS stacks).
* Understanding of host and guest OS power coordination and inter\-VM communication protocols.
* Experience with BSP, device drivers, kernel subsystems, and embedded system architecture on Snapdragon SoCs.
* Experience with power, thermal, and performance characterization of AI, DSP, NSP, or accelerator workloads.
* Experience with system stability, suspend/resume reliability, reboot, shutdown, and watchdog debugging.
* Experience with customer requirements analysis and translation into internal technical specifications.
* Experience creating architecture documentation, debug guides, training materials, and technical workshops.
* Experience using debugging and hardware analysis tools:
* JTAG and TRACE32
* Oscilloscopes and Logic analyzers
* Kernel tracing and logging tools (ftrace, systrace, perf, etc.)
* Performance and power monitoring tools (Trepn, SimplePerf, QPT, etc.)
* Understanding of ARM architecture and embedded SoC hardware: clocks, PLLs, GPIO, interrupts, GIC, power domains, regulators, memory, and subsystem power control.
* Experience with automotive or compute platforms involving digital cockpit, infotainment, ADAS, AI workloads, or vehicle compute systems.
* Experience mentoring engineers and influencing cross\-functional architecture or software decisions.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Information Systems, Computer Science, or related field and 4\+ years of Software Applications Engineering, Software Development experience, or related work experience.

OR
  

Master's degree in Engineering, Information Systems, Computer Science, or related field and 3\+ years of Software Applications Engineering, Software Development experience, or related work experience.
  

OR
  

PhD in Engineering, Information Systems, Computer Science, or related field and 2\+ years of Software Applications Engineering, Software Development experience, or related work experience.
  

  

* 2\+ years of experience with Programming Language such as C, C\+\+, Java, Python, etc.
* 1\+ year of experience with debugging techniques.

There are no technical leads on this team. Everyone is a member of the technical team, and everyone stays hands\-on — senior people included. If you are looking for a title that gets you out of the code, this is not that job.

This role is contributing to the **ABB Installation Products Division** in Electrification Business Area  

.  

You will be mainly accountable for:

* **Building.** Hands\-on development every week — objects, extensions, integrations through OData and REST, and the work to keep them stable afterward.
* **Talking to the business directly.** No ticket queue between you and the person who has the problem. You sit with them, work out what they actually need, and build that — rather than building what a relayed specification said.
* **Using AI openly on the work,** and being accountable for the result. See below.
* **Shipping in small pieces, quickly.** Something small delivered this week beats something complete next quarter.
* **Keeping the quality bar.** Code review, technical documentation, design documents, recovery plans. Owned by the people who build, not enforced by someone else.
* **Security, privacy and governance compliance** on everything you touch.
* **Bringing other developers along** without stepping out of the code yourself.

 **How we work**

* **AI is expected, not tolerated.** The SAP world is conservative about this and we are not. Use assistants for development, debugging, test data, analysis and documentation — openly, and as much as they help.
* Two conditions. You own what you ship: *the model wrote it* is not a defence in code review, and we will ask you to explain generated code line by line. And throughput expectations reflect the fact that you have these tools.
* **Speed over completeness.** We would rather put something small in front of a user this week and learn from it than hand over something finished next quarter that turns out to solve the wrong problem.
* **Small team, high ownership.** Everyone builds and everyone supports. You will not be handed a narrow lane and left in it.
* **Honesty over polish.** Saying "I don't know, here is how I would find out" is a good answer here. Overstating what you have done is not.

 **Where this goes**

* The people who do well on this team end up understanding the business process better than whoever wrote the specification — and then they stop needing the specification.
* If you want to become techno\-functional rather than a career developer, say so in your application. We will put you in requirement sessions, give you process ownership as you earn it, and back you into that transition. We would rather grow you into it than watch you leave to do it somewhere else.

* 3\+ years on S/4HANA, including at least one full implementation.

* Breadth across ERP, EWM, TM or analytics.
* AI experience outside of SAP world
* SAP certifications in ABAP, technical or integration areas.

**About Exotel**

Exotel is the operating system for business communications in emerging markets.



Every day, our platform powers the calls, messages and Voice AI interactions that connect a Bajaj agent to a customer, a Zomato delivery partner to a household, a HDFC banker to a borrower, and a Bolna voicebot to millions of end users.



We process billions of minutes and messages annually across India, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa. We are the substrate underneath one of the fastest\-scaling contact centre and Voice AI ecosystems in the world.

**Own the largest surface we run**
==================================

  



Voice powers thousands of enterprise deployments including HDFC, RBL and international BFSI accounts, and sits underneath the fastest\-growing segment of our business: Voice AI.



It is also the most complex product surface we operate — ExoML APIs, the voice platform, throttling and traffic management, LeadAssist, recording infrastructure, K8S\-based enterprise deployments and real\-time telephony reliability across geographies.



This role is the product owner for that surface.



You define what gets built, why it matters and how success is measured, in close partnership with our Engineering leadership and the go\-to\-market team.



If you want an environment where technical depth is respected, product craft is expected, and the roadmap has real revenue and enterprise weight behind it, this is that seat.

  


**What You Will Own**
=====================

  

* Platform strategy and roadmap \- outcomes, sequencing, and trade\-offs across a 12–18 month horizon. Build ground\-up product stories from customer signals, QBR data, competitive analysis and platform reality. You are not processing inbound requests.
* Platform APIs and payload surface — including AMD, recording status callbacks, disconnectedBy, throttling APIs, and the next generation of programmable platform primitives.
* Enterprise platform deployments
* Cross\-product platform integrations \- with platformbot, CQA, contact centre, and streaming.
* The developer and enterprise customer experience \- including QBR ownership on top 20 accounts and Developer NPS \>45 across the API surface.
* Build ground\-up product stories from customer signals, QBR data, competitive analysis, and platform reality — not just processing inbound requests.

  

**What We’re Looking For**
==========================

  



We care more about what you have actually owned than your previous title.



You have ideally:


* Built real systems as an engineer, and now want to own the product decisions behind them.
* Spent at least 3\-4 years operating in technically complex domains — CPaaS, telephony, developer platforms, API\-first products, data infrastructure or equivalent.
* Read system design docs, held your own in a review with a staff engineer, and known when an engineering estimate is soft.
* Written PRDs engineers actually reference.
* Done real discovery and built user stories from first principles.
* Defended prioritisation with data.

* Known when to move fast and when to wait, when to be direct and when to be diplomatic, when to hold a scope and when to renegotiate.

  




**This Role May Be a Strong Fit If You Are**
--------------------------------------------



A senior or staff engineer considering a product move. If your technical depth is real and your appetite for product craft is genuine, apply and tell us how you are thinking about the transition. We have seen this path produce some of the best technical PMs in our space.

  



A product manager from a CPaaS\-adjacent developer platform — auth, messaging, payments, analytics infrastructure. The domain\-specific telephony knowledge can be built. The platform thinking and API\-product craft cannot.

**This is probably not the right role if:**
-------------------------------------------

  


* Your experience is primarily roadmap execution and processing inbound requests.
* You have not worked in a technically complex domain and do not want to start.
* You need a well\-defined mandate and close supervision to make progress.

The devotion market is a $44B opportunity in India (growing at 10% CAGR), which is primarily offline and unorganised. The Sri Mandir app is the world’s largest app for Hindu devotees and growing 20\-25% month\-on\-month.

  


Try the Sri Mandir app: **Android** / **iOS**
  

  

**Role Overview**


You own **growth and category** for Srimandir's own D2C channel end\-to\-end.
  

It's a full\-loop role: you **generate the demand**, decide the **assortment** (how deep within a category, how wide across categories), set the **price and promotion**, and orchestrate all of it against India's **devotional calendar**, the rhythm that drives this business. You run the store like a P\&L and grow it.


**What you'll own**


**1 · Category — vertical \& horizontal thinking.** Build the assortment on two axes:


* **Vertical (go deep):** depth and premium ladders within winning categories, drive the NPD pipeline (new SKUs, variants, price tiers).
* **Horizontal (go wide):** expand into new categories, cross\-sell and basket expansion — decide what to add, what to scale, and what to cut.

**2 · Pricing \& promotion.** Set the pricing and margin architecture per category; design the discounting, offers and bundling that grow volume without eroding margin.


**3 · Calendar planning.** Build and run the festive / muhurat / seasonal calendar (Sawan, Navratri, Diwali and the rest) as the operating rhythm \- plan launches, campaigns, inventory and promotions against each peak, well ahead of time.

* D2C revenue and growth at or above plan; category contribution up.
* AOV and repeat\-purchase rate rising, with healthy CAC / ROAS.
* Margin held while scaling volume, pricing and promo discipline.
* Calendar\-led launches shipped on time, with demand captured at each festival peak.

**What you bring**


* 4–6 years in category management, growth, or D2C e\-commerce \- **deally a mix of category ownership and demand generation.**
* Performance\-marketing fluency \- run or closely partnered on Meta / Google plus CRM / retention.
* Pricing and P\&L comfort; a sharp assortment / NPD instinct (vertical depth \+ horizontal expansion).
* Data\-driven \- strong analytics; makes decisions from funnel and category data.

* D2C consumer\-brand / FMCG / e\-commerce background; app or store growth experience.
* Feel for festive, seasonal, calendar\-driven categories.
* Affinity for the spiritual / devotional space and Indian consumer nuance (Hinglish a plus).

With the B2B payments market projected to hit US$175 trillion by 2030, Nium offers ambitious builders the chance to shape the future of global money movement with the scale of a leader and the energy of a high\-growth company.

 **About the Role**



Nium moves billions in payments every month for some of the world’s most demanding companies — banks, fintechs, and enterprise platforms operating across 100\+ countries. We built that on fiat rails. The next layer is digital currency: stablecoins, on/off\-ramps, and card products that let customers spend, settle, and move value in USDC as naturally as they do in dollars or euros.



We’re hiring a Staff PM – Digital Assets to own that build. Not the strategy document — the actual product. If you’ve shipped a stablecoin wallet, a crypto\-funded card, or a fiat\-to\-digital conversion flow and you understand what it takes to get that through compliance, engineering, and go\-live in a regulated environment, this is your rol



### **Responsibilities**


* Own stablecoin\-funded card products — physical and virtual cards funded from or settled in stablecoins (USDC and equivalents). Define the product, get it through compliance, ship it.
* Build digital asset support into Nium’s multi\-currency wallet — hold, convert, and send stablecoins alongside fiat currencies. This is a wallet extension, not a new product line.
* Design and ship on/off\-ramp flows — fiat\-to\-digital and digital\-to\-fiat conversion, including rate logic, settlement timing, and failure handling. Own the full customer experience.

* Own compliance product design for digital assets — MiCA, VASP frameworks, travel rule, FinCEN requirements. These get built into the product spec, not handed off to legal.
### **Requirements**

* 7\+ years in product management. Fintech, crypto infrastructure, or payments required.
* You’ve shipped at least one digital asset product in production — a stablecoin wallet, a crypto card, an on/off\-ramp, or a digital settlement rail. Not a prototype. Not a strategy deck.
* Strong payments foundation — cross\-border flows, FX, wallets, settlement mechanics. Digital assets are an extension of this, not a departure from it.
* Regulatory fluency as a product skill — you know what MiCA, travel rule, VASP registration, and FinCEN MSB requirements mean for your spec, your launch sequence, and your go/no\-go decisions.
* Experience working with custodians, blockchain infrastructure, or card networks — enough to evaluate integration tradeoffs and write requirements that engineering can build against.
* Comfortable operating in high\-ambiguity, high\-compliance environments — you know when to move and when to wait for legal sign\-off.
### **How We’ll Measure Success**


* Volume settled on digital rails (stablecoin payins \+ payouts) — tracked quarterly against target
* Card activation rate and spend volume for stablecoin\-funded card products
* On/off\-ramp conversion rate and time\-to\-settlement

title: Delightree - Senior Design Engineer
description:
### **About the role**


This role splits roughly in half.


The first half is designing for franchise operations \- multi location brands, franchisee owners, and frontline staff each needing something different from the same product.


The second half is owning the layer between design and code. You'll own the design system \- the components, patterns, and code. You'll write frontend code yourself, and you'll define how design work becomes a shipped interface for everyone else on the team.


That second half is why this role exists. Our approach to product development is shifting. Instead of traditional mockup handoffs, product managers and designers directly build working prototypes directly in code, using AI workflows alongside our component library. Engineering builds on those prototypes rather than starting over. You own this system and ensure it's up to scale and quality.

### **What you'll do**

* Design and build UI in the same motion \- prototyping novel AI\-native interactions directly in code rather than in Figma\-then\-handoff, especially where no pattern library exists yet.
* Sit inside a pod (PM \+ eng lead \+ you) and take features from concept to shipped, rather than handing off a spec and waiting.
* Own the interaction and motion details \- loading/streaming states, transitions, micro\-interactions \- the polish that's nearly impossible to fully spec in a doc.
* Build and maintain shared UI components so the rest of the org can move fast without reinventing patterns feature by feature.
* Work directly in the production codebase.

### **What we're looking for**

* 4\+ years in product design, with depth in dense interfaces \- tables, forms, permissions, multi role flows.
* Real product/visual design judgment *and* the ability to ship real frontend code \- not a designer who dabbles in code or an engineer who cares about UI, but someone for whom design and implementation are the same skill.
* Hands\-on frontend engineering. A portfolio \+ GitHub showing shipped, interactive, polished products \- not just mockups or case studies.
* Design systems built and maintained at scale, in code. You should be able to direct AI tools to build and maintain prototypes that adhere to accessibility, component system, and other guardrails.
* Experience or strong interest in AI\-native interfaces: streaming output, agentic/human\-in\-the\-loop UX, confidence and uncertainty in UI.
* Bonus: has worked somewhere small enough that design and engineering weren't separate functions. AI used structurally in how features got shipped, from ideation through implementation and review \- not just for copy or asset generation.
